memo.verdict: Park at Triaging, medium-low conviction; do not progress to Early-Stage Assessment now. Not a permanent kill: two named reactivation triggers are set — (1) any credible América Móvil (AMX) stake-reduction/disposal signal, which would remove the driver behind both tripped Element E8 negative guardrails; (2) a Belarus resolution event (managed exit, formal write-down, or material EU sanctions relief), which would remove the Group 4 dominant risk signal. Secondary trigger: if the six-driver count narrows toward four or fewer at the next Change Forces refresh, the Element E7 guardrail finding should be re-tested. TKA-AT moves to the watchlist under cohort 13.286 (Southern and Iberian European telecoms operators, with HTO-GR and NOS-PT), flagged for quarterly re-triage; scheduled re-run at the next Change Forces family-report refresh (~3 months out). The case clears Element E1 on genuine, partially-delivered change forces but fails the double-weighted Element E7 simplicity guardrail and trips both Element E8 negative setup guardrails. This is framed as a park on complexity and risk, not a rejection of business quality — a Belarus-free version of this case would likely progress.
case: Element E1 clears on genuine, partially-evidenced change forces: six independently-ranked drivers, five of six tagged "Independent" (so a Belarusian FX setback would not mechanically impair CEE ICT growth); only Driver 3 (cost efficiency) is flagged as required to offset Driver 2 (Austrian ARPU pressure). International ICT solutions revenue surged 27% in Q2 2025; B2B digital revenue grew at a 19% CAGR FY21-FY24; A1 Bulgaria's fixed broadband share rose from 18% to 27% in 2025 — a durable structural shift. Internal change is genuine and largely already executed: CEO transition from Thomas Arnoldner to Alejandro Plater (Sept 2023) retained continuity since Plater was the group's own CEO 2015-2018; an 18-year workforce programme cut headcount 21% since 2019; the 2023 EuroTeleSites tower spin-off achieved a EUR 1.0bn net debt reduction (completed, not pending).

The robust-base read (E1 RA2) rests on the deleveraging fact as the standout datapoint — net cash of EUR 159m by Q1 2026, down from 1.0x leverage in 2022 — plus a genuinely well-invested network base: ~86% of the Austrian population has 5G coverage, fibre reaches ~95% of municipalities, and a 2.6 GHz spectrum extension cost only EUR 11m versus a EUR 100m commitment required of peers in Serbia. Delivery congruency is broadly strong: FY2025 achieved 114.1% of its internal FCF target and 98.6% of its service revenue target; Q1 2026 EBITDAaL beat consensus by 2.0%. The valuation gap is real on cash-flow terms even if the source report itself argues the discount is largely fundamentally justified: the 2026 unlevered FCF yield of 10.1% trades at a premium to the sector median of 7.7% (Deutsche Bank), and TKA-AT ranked first of six regional peers (KPN, Swisscom, Proximus, Elisa, Telenor, TKA-AT) on Q1 2026 EBITDA momentum.

Thematic fit (E5) is genuinely two-sided but net positive on three of four Required Attributes: recurring, contracted revenue (80% of Austrian mobile core service revenues) plus the near-net-cash balance sheet support downturn resilience; the group sits on the AI-demand-beneficiary side via B2B digital growth and the Exoscale sovereign-cloud platform, with neither source report flagging AI-driven disintermediation risk to core connectivity.
counter_case: The park decision rests on two double-weighted/carve-out Elements failing simultaneously, not a single borderline call. Element E7 (Required Case Simplicity Guardrails, x2 weight) fails outright: six independently-ranked key drivers across seven geographies exceed the four-driver, ten-geography Triaging guardrails: RA3 (zero headwinds) fails because Austrian MVNO competition and Belarusian repatriation restrictions are both live simultaneously; RA4 (handful of change-from-current items) fails because at least four items run concurrently (workforce restructuring, capex tapering, CEE ICT scale-up, the unresolved Belarus overhang). Five distinct currency regimes (EUR, BGN-peg, RSD, MKD-peg, BYR) sit inside the seven-geography footprint; BYR is the only unpegged regime with a documented history of sharp devaluations (2011, 2015). Impact magnitude across the six drivers spans from a modest 2-3% EBITDA contribution (workforce efficiency) to a severe negative 15-20% (Belarusian FX and trapped cash) — a wide dispersion that is harder to weight and track than a narrower set. Against the cohort, TKA-AT sits further from the guardrail than HTO-GR (five drivers, single country) on every one of the three quantifiable Required Attributes.

Element E8 (Fit With Acceptable Case Setups) trips both negative guardrails — described as "genuinely rare," not observed in either cohort peer's own Triaging read. RA7 (unacceptable-setup guardrail, TRIPPED): public shareholders control only 11% of equity and cannot block AMX or ÖBAG capital-allocation decisions — "this guardrail is genuinely tripped, not a marginal call, and should weigh heavily in the park decision." RA8 (false-friend guardrail, TRIPPED): a statistically cheap headline (3.8x EV/EBITDAaL) combined with unresolved structural impairments is a textbook false-friend pattern; the Business Foundation report's own language states the discount "appears fundamentally justified rather than opportunistic," naming Belarus and governance as the offsetting factors — and the 42% discount is wider than the 15-25% historical range for majority-controlled European telecom comparators, itself weak evidence the market has already partly priced the guardrail risk. The historical precedent cited: Société Générale's exit from Rosbank in 2022 completed within weeks of a political trigger, at a EUR 3.2bn write-off — if Belarus crystallises on that timeline rather than gradually, "the cheap 3.8x multiple would reprice sharply lower before any exit-related re-rating could occur." No positive setup among six clears more than a partial fit; the best (RA2, CEE demand growth) alone would likely support only a C.
triggers: - Trigger 1 (primary): any credible América Móvil stake-reduction or disposal signal — would remove the driver behind both tripped Element E8 negative guardrails. A free-float increase toward 30-35% would likely re-grade RA7 toward C, closing roughly half the distance to a clean E8 pass.

- Trigger 2 (primary): Belarus resolution — a managed exit, formal write-down, or material EU sanctions relief — would remove the Group 4 dominant risk signal; even a partial impairment would remove the single largest input feeding the RA8 false-friend read. Both triggers together would very likely clear E8 to a B.

- Trigger 3 (secondary): if the six-driver count narrows toward four or fewer at the next Change Forces refresh (management commentary hints CEE ICT growth and cost efficiency could mature into a single reported driver within 12-18 months), the Element E7 guardrail finding should be re-tested.

- What Early-Stage Assessment would need to resolve if reopened: a specific, quantified Belarus exit-scenario range (managed sale vs forced write-down vs status quo), each with its own EBITDA and book-value impact — named as the single highest-value analytical task; whether the driver count has narrowed toward four; América Móvil's own group-level capital-allocation pressure/Mexican regulatory environment/debt-service needs as read-through on disposal likelihood within a 2-4 year horizon; whether the 19% B2B digital CAGR is durable or partly funding-cycle-dependent.

- Monitoring cadence: standing quarterly monitor on América Móvil capital-allocation disclosures and the EU Belarus sanctions Council calendar; re-run the Triaging pass at the next Change Forces refresh (~3 months). Quarterly: track CEE international service-revenue growth against the 11.5% Q1 2026 print. Semi-annual: review MVNO share against the current 18% plateau — a sustained move above 22% would likely warrant an unscheduled Element E11 re-grade. Named early-warning indicator: a single adverse Bulgarian termination-rate decision would likely signal a broader regulatory-posture shift (cockroach-never-alone model). Reconcile the Q4 2025 consensus miss (EBITDA before restructuring missed by 3.3%) against the honest-tracker delivery narrative at the next refresh. Verify 2026 capex delivery against the EUR 750m guidance at the next quarterly print.

- Named data gaps/discrepancies carried forward unresolved: leverage estimate (IG note ~1.0-1.1x vs HTO-GR peer memo ~2.0x vs Change Forces net cash — Change Forces treated as authoritative); sector FCF yield benchmark (7.7% vs 6.3%, both attributed to Deutsche Bank, not reconciled); Buy rating percentage (50% simple ratio vs 17% dashboard buy_rev, not reconciled); NOS-PT not yet Triaged at family-report depth, so a full three-way simplicity comparison is not yet possible.
